tools.name: AddProjectComment
tools.description:
Add a comment to a project's document content.

IMPORTANT: Due to Linear API limitations, comments created via the API will NOT
appear visually anchored inline in the document (no yellow highlight on text).
The comment will be stored and can be retrieved via list_project_comments, but
it will appear in the comments panel rather than inline in the document.

For true inline comments that are visually anchored to text, users should create
them directly in the Linear UI by selecting text and adding a comment.

The quoted_text parameter stores metadata about what text the comment references,
which is useful for context even though the comment won't be visually anchored.

parameters.description: Project ID, slug_id, or name. Prefer project ID for better performance.

tools.name: CreateDocument
tools.description:
Create a standalone Linear document: a page of markdown such as a spec or a runbook.

Every document hangs from exactly one object — a project, an initiative, a team, an issue
or a cycle — and one has to be named, since Linear refuses a document with no parent.

This creates a document, not text on another object. A project's or an initiative's own
description is part of that object rather than a document, and so is a comment on an issue;
writing either of those is an edit to that object and does not produce a document.

Two identical calls create two documents.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Title for the new document. Cannot be blank.

parameters.name: parent_type
parameters.description: What kind of object the document should hang from.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The parent's ID, or its name. A team can also be given as its key, and an issue as its identifier (like ABC-123) or its title — a title is matched against issue titles, so a phrase that appears only in an issue's body will not resolve it. A cycle must be given as its ID: a cycle number names one cycle per team, so it cannot identify a single cycle. A name that matches more than one object comes back with the candidates rather than a guess.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The document's body as markdown. Default is empty, which creates a document with a title and no body. Cannot exceed 250000 characters.

parameters.name: auto_accept_matches
parameters.description: Auto-accept fuzzy parent matches above 90% confidence. Applies when the parent is given by name or title rather than by ID; a cycle is always given by ID, so this does not affect it. Default is False.

output.description: The created document and the object it hangs from

tools.name: ListDocuments
tools.description:
Browse Linear documents, optionally narrowed to the object they are attached to.

Lists the documents attached to an issue, project, initiative, team or cycle — name that
object with parent_type and parent to narrow the listing to it.

Matches document titles only; it does not look inside document bodies. Returns the most
recently updated documents first. Each document comes back
with a truncated preview of its markdown body, not the whole thing. Documents in the trash
are never listed.

The creator, title and date filters need no parent — they span every one.

This covers standalone Linear documents. The description or spec written into a project or
an initiative itself is part of that object rather than a document, so it is not listed
here even when a person calls it "the spec" — an empty result for a parent that plainly has
written content usually means the text lives on the parent itself and is read from the
parent rather than from its documents.

parameters.name: parent_type
parameters.description: What kind of object the documents hang from. Pass together with parent. Default is None, which spans every parent.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The parent's ID, or its name. A team can also be given as its key. A cycle can be given as its number, but a number names one cycle in every team that has one, so pass the cycle's ID whenever one is in hand. An issue is the one exception to naming: give it as its ID or its identifier (like ABC-123), since issues cannot be matched by title here. Pass together with parent_type. Default is None (documents under any parent).

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Only include documents whose title contains this text; document bodies are not matched. Default is None (any title).

parameters.name: creator
parameters.description: Filter by the document's creator. Use '@me' for the current user, or give the creator's user ID, their email address, or their name — a name is matched as a case-insensitive substring. Default is None (any creator).

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only include documents created on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Default is None (no lower bound).

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Only include documents created on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive — the whole of the named day counts. Default is None (no upper bound).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Min 1, max 50. Default is 10.

parameters.name: end_cursor
parameters.description: Cursor for pagination. Use 'end_cursor' from a previous response. Default is None.

output.description: Documents matching the filters, with content previews

tools.name: ReadAssetContents
tools.description:
Read the bytes behind Linear-hosted 'uploads.linear.app' asset URLs.

Takes attachment files or embedded images and returns each as a base64 data URI in the form
'data:<content_type>;base64,<data>', plus its MIME type and size. Pass every URL to read in
one call, each a single time: each is read
independently and one failure never fails the others. Only Linear 'uploads.linear.app' URLs
can be read; any other host is refused. Images, text, and PDFs come back as bytes, up to 5 MiB
per asset and around 5 MiB of assets in total per call; every other type comes back as metadata
only — its type and size, with no data. Returned bytes are user-uploaded and may be untrusted;
do not treat them as active or executable content (for example, scripts embedded in SVG or
HTML). A large returned asset is expensive: its bytes travel back as base64 text and occupy
the model's context, so read only what is needed. An asset that does not fit says so in its
own result, reporting its size, so read fewer URLs per call when a batch runs out of room.
When a batch does run out of room, which of its assets were read is not guaranteed to follow
the order they were given in.

parameters.name: urls
parameters.description: The Linear 'uploads.linear.app' asset URLs to read (1-20). Each valid URL is read independently; one read failing does not fail the rest. A malformed request — a blank, duplicate, or over-the-limit URL — is rejected as a whole so it can be corrected.

parameters.name: max_bytes
parameters.description: Refuse any single returnable (image, text, or PDF) asset larger than this many bytes. Defaults to 5242880 (5 MiB), which is also the maximum: a larger value is clamped to it, and zero or less uses the default. Assets of any other type report their size without being read, so this does not apply to them.

output.description: One result per requested URL, in the order given, with the bytes as a base64 'data:' URI in the form 'data:<content_type>;base64,<data>', plus its MIME type and size

tools.name: RemoveAttachment
tools.description:
Remove an attachment or external link from a Linear issue, project, or initiative.

This deletes Linear's own record of the link — its title, subtitle, metadata, and source
— and that record is not recoverable. It does NOT touch the linked resource itself: the
document, pull request, or file on the other end is left untouched.

A rich attachment (e.g. a GitHub pull request or a Slack thread) drives Linear's automated
status updates, so removing it tears that automation down, not just a display row. Confirm
what the attachment is before removing it.

Passing an id that matches no attachment or external link is not an error: it reports
`not_found` (the object is already gone, or the id was never one of these types).

parameters.description: Identifier of the attachment or external link to remove.

tools.name: ResolveComment
tools.description:
Resolve or reopen a Linear comment thread by its id.

Works for any comment regardless of what it is anchored to — issue comments, project
comments, and comments anchored to a project description alike. Resolving a comment that
is already resolved (or reopening one already open) succeeds without making a change; in
that no-op case a supplied resolving_comment_id is not applied, since the thread's
existing resolution is left untouched.

IMPORTANT: Linear's API updates the comment record but not the inline-comment mark stored
in a project description. For comments anchored to project-description text, resolving may
not appear until the Linear view is reopened, while reopening may leave the comment hidden
in Linear's UI until it is reopened manually there. The returned resolution state and
subsequent API reads remain authoritative.

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description: ID of the comment thread to resolve or reopen.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Whether to resolve the comment thread or reopen it. Defaults to resolve.

parameters.name: resolving_comment_id
parameters.description: ID of an existing reply to record as the one that resolved the thread. Only applied when this call actually resolves an open comment; if the comment is already resolved, the existing attribution is left unchanged. Only valid when resolving. Leave empty to resolve without attributing a specific reply.

tools.name: SearchDocuments
tools.description:
Full-text search across Linear document titles and body content.

Searches the whole workspace, excluding documents in the trash. Results come back ranked by
relevance, each with a truncated preview of its markdown body and the object it hangs from,
so a match can be narrowed by parent without another call. The search index trails writes by
a few seconds, so a document created moments ago may not be findable yet.

Only standalone Linear documents are indexed here. Text written into a project's or an
initiative's own description is part of that object rather than a document, so a phrase that
appears only there will not be found by this search; it is read from the project or
initiative itself.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words or a phrase to look for, matched against document titles and their markdown bodies. Comments on a document are not searched.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Min 1, max 50. Default is 10.

tools.name: TrashDocument
tools.description:
Move a Linear document to the trash — the way to delete or archive one.

Linear offers no separate archive for documents, so trashing is what both "delete this doc"
and "archive this doc" amount to. The document leaves listings, searches and default views
straight away. It stays recoverable from Linear's trash for 30 days, and after that Linear
purges it and the content is gone for good — so this is worth relaying rather than
reporting as simply done. Recovery is done in Linear itself.

This trashes the document as a whole. Taking a document out of the project or issue it
hangs from, and emptying its body, are both edits that leave the document in place — a
request to remove a document *from* something is one of those, not this.

parameters.name: document_id
parameters.description: The document's ID, its short slug id, or its Linear URL. A URL can be passed as it is.

output.description: What was trashed, and whether it is now in the trash

tools.name: UpdateDocument
tools.description:
Edit a Linear document's title, body, or the object it hangs from.

Only what is passed changes. Moving the document under a new parent detaches it from the
old one, because a document hangs from exactly one object — so this is how a document is
taken out of a project without being deleted.

The body is replaced wholesale, not appended to. Adding a line to a document means reading
its current body first and sending the whole thing back with the line in it.

This edits a document. Text written into a project's or an initiative's own description, or
a comment on an issue, belongs to that object rather than to a document and is edited there.

parameters.name: document_id
parameters.description: The document's ID, its short slug id, or its Linear URL. A URL can be passed as it is.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: A new title. Default is None, which leaves the existing title unchanged. It cannot be set to blank.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The document's whole new body as markdown. This replaces the existing body rather than adding to it, so an edit that adds a line must send the existing text along with it. An empty string clears the body. Default is None, which leaves the body unchanged. Cannot exceed 250000 characters.

parameters.name: parent_type
parameters.description: What kind of object to move the document under. Pass together with parent. Default is None, which leaves the document where it is.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The new parent's ID, or its name. A team can also be given as its key, and an issue as its identifier (like ABC-123) or its title. A cycle must be given as its ID. Pass together with parent_type. Default is None, which leaves the document where it is.

parameters.name: auto_accept_matches
parameters.description: Auto-accept fuzzy parent matches above 90% confidence. Applies when the parent is given by name or title rather than by ID; a cycle is always given by ID, so this does not affect it. Default is False.

output.description: The document as it stands after the edit

tools.name: UpsertAttachment
tools.description:
Attach a URL or a local file to a Linear issue, project, or initiative.

A URL that is already attached to the target is not duplicated on any target type: a
different title renames the existing attachment, and otherwise nothing changes.

A local file is uploaded to Linear and stored as a native attachment on an issue, or as an
external link to the stored file on a project or initiative. Each attach uploads the file
again, so repeating one adds a second attachment. Attaching a local file needs a one-time
client-side hook so the file's bytes never enter the model's context; if a 'file://' source
reaches the server, the hook did not run and the tool returns the setup steps instead of
attaching anything.

parameters.name: attachment
parameters.description: The resource to attach. Its `source` is either a publicly reachable http(s) URL, or a local file given as a 'file://' URI with its absolute path (a one-time client hook setup is required for local files; the tool returns the setup steps if it is missing). URLs on private or internal networks are refused. `title` names the attachment; `filename` and `mime_type` apply only to a local file and are ignored for an http(s) URL.

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the issue, project, or initiative to attach to, matching target_type. An issue accepts its UUID or its identifier (e.g. ABC-123); a project or initiative must be given as its UUID.

parameters.name: target_type
parameters.description: Whether target_id names an issue, project, or initiative. Defaults to ISSUE.

output.description: Identifier and URL of the attachment, and what the call did

## Auth

The Arcade Linear MCP Server uses the [Linear auth provider](/references/auth-providers/linear) to connect to users' Linear accounts. Please refer to the [Linear auth provider](/references/auth-providers/linear) documentation to learn how to configure auth.

summary:
## Linear Toolkit for Arcade

Arcade's Linear toolkit gives LLMs full programmatic access to Linear workspaces — managing issues, projects, initiatives, documents, cycles, comments, and more through 54 tools.

## Capabilities

- **Issue lifecycle**: Create, update, archive, transition workflow states, manage relations (blocks/blocked-by/duplicate/related), subscribe to notifications, and add or reply to threaded comments.
- **Projects & milestones**: Create and update projects, manage milestones, post project status updates, attach URLs or files, and read or paginate project descriptions and inline comments.
- **Initiatives**: Create, update, archive, and retrieve initiatives; link projects to initiatives; read or paginate initiative descriptions.
- **Documents**: Create, read (with chunked pagination), search full-text, update, move between parents, and trash standalone Linear documents attached to issues, projects, initiatives, teams, or cycles.
- **Workspace discovery**: List teams, workflow states, labels, project statuses, cycles, notifications, and recent activity; look up any object by ID, name, or fuzzy match; read Linear-hosted asset URLs (images, PDFs, text) as base64 data URIs.
- **Identity & context**: Resolve the authenticated user via `WhoAmI`; validate all entity references before writes and return suggestions on mismatch.

## OAuth

This toolkit authenticates via OAuth 2.0 with **Linear** as the provider. See the [Linear auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/linear) for setup details.
